enonce_intro_markdown:
**(i)** A discrete random variable, $X$, is such that $X \sim \mathrm{Bin}(8, p)$.

Given that $\mathrm{Var}(X) = 1.28$,
incertitudes: Question 5 : les points ne sont imprimés que par bloc, « (7 marks) » pour la partie (i) (a, b) et « (6 marks) » pour la partie (ii) (c, d et la question finale sur 3 minutes), soit 13 ; ils ne sont donc pas reportés sur les sous-questions (points null).

Question 5 (ii) : la dernière question (« Find, also, the probability that during a particular 3 minutes interval, no person will enter the supermarket ») n'a pas de lettre imprimée ; elle est numérotée « ii.e » par suite logique (après (c) et (d)). Le sujet imprime « a Poisson distribution with mean 2 » : lu comme une moyenne de 2 personnes par minute, d'où une moyenne de 6 sur 3 minutes.

questions.corrige_markdown:
For $X \sim \mathrm{Bin}(n, p)$ the variance is $\mathrm{Var}(X) = np(1 - p)$. With $n = 8$:

$$8p(1 - p) = 1.28 \;\Longrightarrow\; p(1 - p) = 0.16 \;\Longrightarrow\; p^2 - p + 0.16 = 0$$

$$p = \frac{1 \pm \sqrt{1 - 0.64}}{2} = \frac{1 \pm 0.6}{2} \;\Longrightarrow\; p = 0.2 \ \text{ or } \ p = 0.8.$$

**$p = 0.2$ or $p = 0.8$** (both are valid probabilities; $0.2 \times 0.8 = 0.16$).

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) evaluate $P(X = 5)$, for the smaller value of $p$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The smaller value is $p = 0.2$, so $X \sim \mathrm{Bin}(8, 0.2)$ and $P(X = r) = \binom{8}{r} p^r (1 - p)^{8 - r}$.

$$P(X = 5) = \binom{8}{5}(0.2)^5(0.8)^3 = 56 \times 0.00032 \times 0.512 = 0.00917504$$

**$P(X = 5) = 0.00918$** (to 3 significant figures).

questions.enonce_markdown:
**(ii)** The number of people entering a supermarket per minute follows a Poisson distribution with mean 2.

Find the probability that during a particular minute,

(c) exactly 3 people will enter the supermarket.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $X$ be the number of people entering in one minute, $X \sim \mathrm{Po}(2)$, with $P(X = r) = \dfrac{e^{-\lambda}\lambda^r}{r!}$ and $\lambda = 2$.

$$P(X = 3) = \frac{e^{-2}\,2^3}{3!} = \frac{8e^{-2}}{6} = \frac{4e^{-2}}{3} = 0.18045\ldots$$

**$P(X = 3) = 0.1804$** (to 4 decimal places).

questions.enonce_markdown: (d) at least 3 people will enter the supermarket.
Find, also, the probability that during a particular 3 minutes interval, no person will enter the supermarket.
questions.corrige_markdown:
People enter at an average rate of $2$ per minute, so over $3$ minutes the number $Y$ of entrants has a Poisson distribution with mean $\lambda = 3 \times 2 = 6$ (the sum of independent Poisson variables is Poisson with the sum of the means). Hence $Y \sim \mathrm{Po}(6)$.

$$P(Y = 0) = \frac{e^{-6}\,6^0}{0!} = e^{-6} = 0.0024788\ldots$$

**$P(\text{no person in 3 minutes}) = e^{-6} = 0.00248$** (to 3 significant figures).

(Equivalently, $\left[P(X = 0)\right]^3 = \left(e^{-2}\right)^3 = e^{-6}$.)
